ledger.x: 14 July 1958: a coup led by Abdul Karim Qasim overthrows the monarchy and Iraq becomes a republic.
February 1963: the Ba'ath party takes power in a coup.
17 July 1968: the Ba'ath returns to power.
1975: Iraq cedes the eastern bank of the Shatt al-Arab to Iran under the Algiers Agreement.
22 September 1980: Iraq invades Iran along 'a 644 km front'.
1982: Iraq takes its share of the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone.
23 July 1983: Iran takes the Iraqi town of Haj Omran.
20 August 1988: the cease-fire ends the Iran-Iraq War and Haj Omran returns to the pre-war line.
20 August 1988: the cease-fire ends the Iran-Iraq War and Majnoon Island returns to the pre-war line ('Status quo ante bellum'; 'The war did not create any permanent border changes').
2 August 1990: Iraq invades and annexes Kuwait.
26 February 1991: the Iraqi occupation of Kuwait ends.
1992: Baghdad loses control of Iraqi Kurdistan.
15 October 2005: the Kurdistan Region becomes a federal region of Iraq.
2005: Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic row ends and its 'Republic of Iraq' row resumes only in 2014.

wars.name: Kuwait crisis of 1961 (Operation Vantage)
wars.outcome: Iraq threatened to invade Kuwait in July 1961; the invasion 'was finally averted following plans by the Arab League to form an international Arab force' and British forces had withdrawn by 19 October.

wars.name: Iran-Iraq War
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: 22 September 1980 to 20 August 1988, 'Status quo ante bellum'; 'The war did not create any permanent border changes'.

wars.name: Invasion of Kuwait and Gulf War
wars.outcome: Iraq annexed Kuwait on 2 August 1990 as its 19th governorate; a US-led coalition ground assault of 100 hours ended the occupation on 26 February 1991.

wars.name: 1991 Iraqi uprisings and the no-fly zones
wars.outcome: The uprisings 'were repressed', but the US, UK, Turkey and France set up the Iraqi no-fly zones under Security Council Resolution 688 and 'autonomy was given to Kurds': the Kurdistan Region was de facto established in 1992.

wars.name: 2003 invasion of Iraq
wars.outcome: 'On 20 March 2003, the US-led coalition invaded Iraq'; the Kurdistan page says it 'overthrew Saddam Hussein'.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow treaty and survey lines (the 1932 Kuwait line, the Algiers Agreement line of 1975 on the Shatt al-Arab).

National frontiers as before, after the UN demarcation of the Kuwait border (accepted November 1994); the line of the de facto Kurdistan Region, held from 1992, is a front, not a survey: soft, and Kirkuk stayed disputed.
